This game wreaks of the initial essence of The Isle- but with modern-day creatures. It definitely is in need of intense refinement and fine-tuning, but as it stands as an uncompleted game still currently in development... it is indeed one to invest in. There are pros and cons to this game, and sadly the first being- it is probably... at the level of development that it is currently at... not worth the money asking for it. The developers would have a much more devout following and support had they simply done a Kickstarter and offered a key for beta testers that donated- rather than asking for... what was it... $19.99 USD? I don't remember, honestly. It could have been $10 and I would say the same. Something like this, that is no better than a free mobile game due to it's early access lack of finesse, should not be as expensive as this. I doubt even The Isle was this expensive in Early Access times.

The next con- is the overall 'battle system'. I put it in quotes because- lets face it- when something circles around back... it's near impossible to turn around to attack back. Just have to roll over and let an infant water buffalo AI murder your adult lion- because THEY also cause bleed with every attack... which is 30 seconds of bleed PER BLEED. I had an adult lion bleeding with 12 bleed from an infant water buffalo because it just stayed behind me, and I couldn't turn around to kill it. You think "Run away- and turn around!" NO. The AI MATCH YOUR SPEED- you run? They run. You stop? They saunter up behind you and bite your bum. You try to turn? Guess what? They're magicians- the lot of them! They can slide- so that their rumps are NEVER facing you! Always on the attack! It's magical!

The next con is the general wonkiness of eating and drinking. It's not a big one like the other two, but it still needs hella work. (look I'm dropping my 'educated' verbiage since, if you made it this far, your brain is not necessarily running on all cylinders like mine is at the moment) SOMETIMES, the press and hold E to eat/drink works. As a cub- as an adolescent- as a young adult and as a non-elder adult... the E to drink needed to be pressed, held and wait to take a sip... then let go, wait a few seconds... pressed, held and wait to take a sip... rinse and repeat until full. If you're not positioned right over the food... even though it says Press E to Eat. It doesn't register unless you're on that sweet spot... which... oftentimes... sphincter was on the menu. Like groceries, my dudes. Like groceries.

Another, lesser, con I guess... are the lengthy nights. The Isle has this issue too... but the servers, even if you're in your own alone, don't even give you the option to shorten these. I was a cub going into the snowy night- and finally when the day broke, I was literally an adult. If that's not a good example of how freakin' long these nights are- I don't know what is.

LAST CON to this before we get to the good stuff is... THERE'S LITERALLY NOTHING AROUND FOR MILES. Like good LORD. I ran until I found the world border- and there were no AI... no water bits... nothing really of any significance. I found a crashed plane once- and a rock formation that resembled male genitalia. But nothing HAPPENED at them- there was no easter eggs or anything cool for being there... not even spawn points for AI prey to eat. Just... vast amounts of nothingness. The open world roaming is definitely appreciated- but if it's going to be THAT big, and if they're going to be THAT slow... give more spawn points- or REWARD the player for venturing forth! I only ever saw Water Buffalo. When I was that hawk- that couldn't drink or eat, mind you- I saw rhinos. But that's it. If that's supposed to be Africa? I'm FAIRLY certain it's TEEMING with wildlife. (Also- I love the touch with the little black birds, and having them fly off if you run through them? But I'm really sad you can't kill them for a quick meal.)

BUT there are also Pros for this game! It's absolutely beautiful. I couldn't stop taking screenshots (most were at night because... as you recall... the nights last forever. It's like it takes place in Alaska!) But the level of detail, even in the skybox itself- I'm not even entirely sure it IS a skybox from how responsive the lighting was! When a cloud moved in front of the super bright moon- it actually got darker... the moon moved across the sky and so the point of light differed from when it was high in the sky to when it was nearly morning time... and my most favorite was sunrise! It was absolutely gorgeous!

Another Pro- are the options to choose from for your creatures,  you don't HAVE to start out as a baby (although I only played on a solo server just to get the feel of everything before jumping head-first into online play, so it may be different on 'official' servers.) While it is ideal to, so you can have control over how powerful your creature is... it isn't necessary to start out as an infant. If you just want to play without wasting HOURS (like in The Isle on progression) you can start at the top! The Isle also has this, though... it's "sandbox mode"... however this seems to be the default for this game, and I love it!

Another Pro is the customization, but this pro comes hand-in-hand with a slight con, as well. While the ability to customize your creature so no two creatures look EXACTLY the same is awesome, I love this aspect about ARK and how you can make the most grotesque human character you could fathom... but the only con in this happens to be the viewing box. The controls in the top right specify: "Left Click moves the screen around", "Right Click adjusts the screen up and down" and "Scroll/Middle Mouse Button zooms in and out". Well... sorry to break it to you... left and right do the same exact things. There is no "adjusting the screen up and down" It's just "You spin me right 'round baby right 'round" all night long. I couldn't see WHAT I was adjusting and ended up with a lioness with an INCREDIBLY long snoot- massive paws, and a middle so thin- her hind legs went concave when she laid down. So while this is a PRO for customization- it definitely needs A LOT of work (not to mention way more OBVIOUS patterns to work with... the lion has 4 and the only one that looked even remotely different was like, a slightly more brown coat. I get it- lions aren't very diverse in their colors... but sometimes they kinda deserve that drastic difference like Zira and Scar from the Lion King!)

The last Pro I can think of is the leveling system! This is entirely different from any other play-as-creature survival-like game. (Discounting ARK-) If you start as an infant, you gain points- I believe 30 at first- to put into whatever you like; health, stamina, oxygen, attack, and even armor! It's interesting to see- since usually in these games- either you're stronk against something, or you're not and you need to run away fast. But now- even as an herbivore- you can pump up the attack and armor- and kick a pack of lion's butts! Probably. Again, I only played as the birb and the Lioness.

In either case- make your better judgement. I couldn't chose a neutral suggestion for "recommend this game for others" but I don't necessarily think people SHOULDN'T give it a go. It's in your best interest to read through this thoroughly- see other's takes on it as well with other reviews... and make your choice. Your money- your choice. I won't ask for a refund? Because it has potential... so long as the Developers aren't like how a review said they were and "don't listen to their community" because that would be stupid and disastrous on their ends.

Of course unless they end up being like "Day of Dragons" developer- and take the money from steam and run... leaving a half-baked pre-made asset-filled mobile rip-off 'game' that they ignored any good suggestions and refused to consider reviews, negative or otherwise; that leaves a bad taste in everyones mouths. :) But lets hope not, right?

Animalia is a fantastic game that lets you step into the paws, claws, or hooves of various animals and experience their world firsthand. Whether you’re sneaking through forests, hunting for food, or exploring vast landscapes, the game offers a unique perspective that’s both immersive and fun.

Playing as different animals adds variety and keeps gameplay fresh, while the environments feel alive and vibrant. The mechanics are intuitive and the freedom to roam and interact with nature makes for a peaceful yet engaging experience.

While it may not have a super deep story or complex objectives, Animalia shines in letting players feel connected to nature and its creatures. It’s a great game for animal lovers and anyone wanting a chill, exploratory adventure.

Pros:

Play as a variety of animals with unique abilities

Beautiful, immersive natural environments

Relaxed and intuitive gameplay

Great for exploration and casual play

Cons:

Can feel a bit repetitive after a while

Lacks complex challenges or objectives

If you’ve ever wanted to see the world from an animal’s point of view, Animalia is a charming and enjoyable journey you won’t want to miss.

I've only played this for a few hours at this point, and I really like the idea/premise of the game. I'm not a HUGE fan of multiplayer so this was kind of a new venture for me. I liked Wolf Quest and thought this struck similarly in that you play and survive as the animal. 

Pros:
 - Cool and interesting concept
 - Beautiful animals 
 - Fun (though limited) game play

Cons:
 - I feel a little biased since I prefer solo game experience, but I'm gonna say this anyway. I don't like the singularly multiplayer experience. I think it's cool as an option, but that there should be maps/quests/game play available that solo players can enjoy because, as I said, the concept of the game is really cool.
 - I struggled playing as the lion to find AI food sources. Had to leave and reload several times for any to spawn. Younger versions of the lion require a significantly higher amount of food/water than the adult lion and that's a problem when there's no food around. 
 - "Attack" actions need work. It's very odd chasing another animal, chomping and clawing and never seeing any slowed or impacted reaction from the AI. I tried to take down a zebra as a sub lion and it took FOREVER. Hunger bar is decreasing constantly the whole time. Can't give up and find something smaller because there's nothing else around. 
 - Joining servers was not a good experience for me. None of my needs showed on the side panel. I spawned as a baby lion and, again, no food or anything around. Traveled, looking for "scent" trails, until finally starving to death. Next time was killed, again as a cub, within two minutes by another player. 

Overall, I think the game play as it stands might appeal to some people; multiplayer is popular. If you like a more solo/immersive experience, the current version of this game isn't for you.

Animalia Survival is bringing my childhood fantasies to reality. Ever since I was younger, I always played animal games, but my favourite aspect was always doing some sort of realistic sim with it. One of the things I did the most often was creating a biome with Zoo Tycoon 2, populating it with it's proper animals, and then going into zookeeper mode and just living life. Animalia Survival is literally that, but with stunning graphics, and other people. I therefor have to strongly recommend to any other person that used to do the same or similar things to definitely grab this one, but there's a catch.

The [b]Single player[/b] mode is uneventful, last time I tried the landscape was devoid of any NPCs or anything to give that herd/pack feeling or even find food for carnivores (? unsure about this one, if you typically play carnivore, feel free to correct me on this). I'm unsure at the time if NPCs actually spawn or not. Either way, solo mode isn't good for much, except getting a feel for the controls.


[b]Multiplayer[/b] is iffy as well, in a very different way. It depends on if you like to play carnivore or herbivore better, and ALSO depends on if the server you're joining has rules.

Carnivore's are pretty rough at the start, unless you join in with a group, because as a pup/cub, you can't really hunt much. But I find that balances the game a bit more, no complaints. Herbivores, on the other hand, as long as you find a quiet spot, you can probably grow to adulthood/elder on an isolated part of the map, emphasis on the isolated part.

The reason a lot of the smaller species can survive in the wild is the sheer number of them. Survival is rooted in their large groups. Therefor, when over 50% of a server is playing as a carnivore and basically you're being attacked all the time by different groups, makes the few people who actually prefer herbivore have an infuriating time. 

[i]"Why not just go to an other server then?"[/i] you may ask yourself. I wish it was as simple as that, as there's usually only a few servers at a time with over 5 people, and with the size of the maps, you do want interaction. Don't get me wrong! I do love a good chase and squabble, then both go off and lick our wounds, or one of us dies, it's life, it's what I want. But, when two different predator groups gang up on you, it's annoying. When you spawn in and you get killed within a minute or two by a group of predators, it's annoying. 

The strength of the animals, I feel, reflect their real life counterparts. The only problem with that is, with the low amount of people playing herbivores in game, you get none of the support. They see one or two gazelles and it's fresh meat, not a risk at all. A zebra versus a group of predators is no big deal. The larger herbivores don't seem to have this problem, as the risk is higher. 

I've been in a few servers where the rules definitely evened things out, like, if a carnivore is currently hunting something, only them & their group can hunt it. So if you're being chased by a solo leopard, a group of 5 lions can't join in. But there isn't that security in numbers, as most people still would play the larger herbivores or any of the carnivores.

Which sucks, because one of the moments I cherish the most about this game is when me and a stranger ended up going from a group of 2 gazelles, to like 15. When we were in a group that large, most solo predators would think twice before attacking, and when a group of lioness' started chasing us, it flustered them more then if they had 1 target. We even managed to kill a croc by ourselves.

An other large downside with it, is that unlike some other multiplayer games, there's no way to tell how experienced a player is. The first time I played, I didn't realise you could change your spawn, and I kept spawning in as a wildebeest, and kept getting killed every time I tried making a new character. So I switched to a lion cub, as they were a lion, and they killed me yet again.


[h1]TLDR[/h1]
Single player is pretty dull, Multiplayer needs to balance things out a bit, and as usual for any multiplayer games, ganking will happen.

If you like playing carnivore, you'll probably have a ton of fun. If you like playing herbivores, good luck out there.

Take everything I say with a grain of salt, as this is still early access, and can therefor change at  any time.

1: The CLUNKINESS. This game has been out for years and there is still trouble a LOT of times where you will have to readjust your character in game to get a sip of water or eat some food, which might not sound bad until you realize it happens double digit times per play session. Then for herbivores you have disappearing plant glitch A LOT as well which makes survival even harder as you should've gotten fed for that plant but when you hold E (your eat button) it instantly disappears. Then you have the water glitch on certain animal skins which means you cant swim in water because you drop directly down... and guess what? IT AFFECTS TWO of the crocodile skins where you'll be in the water a good amount.

Overall I'm having a good time with friends testing out different builds/animals but there are a lot of times that can be frustrating especially when you're on a birth in character that dies due to rule breaking. Animalia Survival is an MMO survival game that takes place in Africa and lets you try to survive as various available African animals. The game is in Early Access, so just about everything in it is somewhat broken, janky or just plain doesn't work properly. But if you persevere you may still get some fun out of the product.

The game is mainly an MMO game. There is an option to host your own server or play solo, but there's literally no point to it beyond testing all the animals available. There are basically no animals on the map outside certain locations and the AI is so brain dead that minecraft zombies seem absolutely, positively bright in comparison. So if when you're playing I very much suggest that you get the game for the MMO aspect alone. At least for now. This might change in the future.

The game is pretty rough though. The animals all look pretty good, but the maps or the only map that I could find, called "TestLevel" is absolutely awful. It's extremely laggy and poorly optimized for something that is mostly just open plains and rolling hills. This will most likely get better as the game chugs along further in its development. After all it's a "test level" and there will most likely be countless changes and optimizations done to it along the way.

Most of the available animals in the game are fully functional. Meaning they have all the different stages of life, starting from a tiny baby and ranging all the way up to the full adult, as well as both sexes. But some of them, such as Vultures and Zebras for example, don't have more than one available option at this point.

Some of the animations for the animals are also pretty stiff and unnatural, but mostly all the animals move around looking nice and proper and perfectly fluid. The worst offenders seem to be sprinting animations and jumping which can look really weird at times.

The animals all have different calls as well. You can make your presence known by pressing 1 as all the other players nearby will hear your call and it can potentially help you find other players of your own species or attract predators that are looming about. There are other calls as well, from friendly to threatening to submissive. But it seems not every animal have all the same calls at this point of the development. Some of them have only three calls and some of them can have up to five. Baby steps.

While in game you have no way of telling if an animal you encounter is a player or an AI. You can't see any name tags and the only way to know is to observe how the animal acts. There's a chat option for global and group chat though, so you can talk to people if you wish. You can though group up with other players. When you group up you can see the name of the player above the animal so you'll instantly know who is in your group. I like this, as it keeps other players anonymous to you. Unless they kill you of course. Then you'll get a message telling who actually killed you.

The gameplay loop is pretty simple. It is basically just survival of the fittest. Your only objective is to have fun and stay alive. You're either eating, drinking or running away from predators or hunting another player as a predator to be your next meal. That's about it. There is though a birthing system in the game. Two adult animals can mate, allowing the female to give birth to baby animals of their respected species. These animals need a player to fill the slot though, so no birthing of AI babies. The herd then has to take care of their young and keep the babies safe until they're old enough to take care of themselves.

It was pretty thrilling as a leopard to surprise attack a large pack of wildebeest from a hiding spot and concentrate my effort on taking down one of their two babies for my starving stomach. It is also surprisingly fun to try and survive as a herbivore and I find myself switching roles after each cycle of life I've had.

Mostly all the action focuses around the food and water sources. Herbivores need grass and plants to eat and water to drink. Carnivores need to hunt herbivores and also drink to stay alive. As players eat and drink, the lakes will run dry and the food will slowly disappear. This forces the herds to migrate to other locations on the map, keeping the game somewhat fresh so that people won't just camp around the same places all the time. Then when it rains the lakes and rives will fill up with water again and new food will grow and the cycle begins a new.

Though, the fun here is very subjective. I think the game needs a certain type of a personality who enjoys this kind of gameplay. I don't think the game is that suitable for an average player who just wants to jump on a server and start murdering people left and right.

This brings me to the biggest downside of the game so far. You won't be having fun unless the server you play on is populated enough. The game is so bare bones right now and there is so little to do that without human interaction you might as well not play the game at all. All the most populated servers also have strict rules about what you can and cannot do while playing. This is to keep the  game fun and fair for everyone and also to balance the animals so that you don't get a storm of lions killing absolutely everything from one end of the map to the other. These rules are at the same time a boon and an annoyance. But that's fine with me. There also seems to be only two servers that are decently populated. The Circle of Life and The Serengeti. All the other servers when I've been itching to play have been ghost towns.

I also strongly suggest you play with a friend if you can. It can be extremely lonely out there otherwise, unless you're willing to group up with other players, which I highly encourage you to do. It's fun to move as a pack or a herd and there's safety in numbers.

Still after all this I find it difficult to recommend the game right now. It is just so unfinished that you really need to be able to see past all the jankyness and issues the game has to be able to have any fun. The performance is god awful, the game lags like crazy, disconnects constantly or just bugs out all the time. There's a huge potential here, but then again, I'm getting a little tired of games with potential that never seems to manifest. Though, I'm eagerly waiting to hear more about the development. Especially after they add hyenas into the game, because hyenas just rock.

I'm going to recommend the game, but that's only because there's no in between option. I suggest that if you're on the fence about getting the game, then you should probably just wait for a little bit longer. Or who knows, get the game now. Maybe after if you decide to wait for just a little bit longer there are no populated servers to play on. I can never tell with Early Access games if they're going to hit it big or fizzle out into obscurity.

Nevertheless, I'm going to keep on playing in small bursts.

TL;DR

A hesitant recommendation. The game is only fun with people. Don't try to host a solo game. Full of bugs. Very bare bones. Awful performance. Though there's potential.

Animalia, currently it's fairly fun if you're lucky and meet fair players. The solo play is very lacking and you can only live a full life on multiplayer where you can find a player as a mate and then birth real players as your offspring and raise them. One of the most popular servers is pretty bad to play on, but one has enough active friendly mods and admins who are fair and the rules are pretty clear and make the game more fun. 

I love that you can climb trees as a leopard which I have wanted a good playable leopard in a game for a long time. And they added scavenging from carcasses to be easier. 

 Animalia still feels like a work in progress, but much of the game is good and since the last time I played I definitely see the improvements, of course making the foundations of the game are most important, so bugs and imbalances should be the devs main focus.
However, I know solo mode would be a huge thing if it was improved.  Like when I think of a playable singleplayer, make the world more immersive with intelligent ai where you can have a completely ai family and ai prey and predators living their own lives and dealing with eachother as well as the player, and also hope in the future they implement more african climate where there is a rainy season when most prey have babies, and also a dry season when things are more difficult and water sources dry up. Building homes would be cool too, especially meerkat colonies. And with warthogs, african wild dogs and hyenas to be able to repurpose old burrows and expand them to their needs. 
Please make group limits per species an admin setting, as well as character slots. More admin settings in general to better customize servers or control your solo save would be a huge thing to consider. 
Perhaps make the points also be able to go towards perks/abilities instead of just improving basic skills, for example burrowing animals be able to make a burrow on their own without needing to use an old one, another perk/ability could be for scent tracking to be easier, or small herbivores being able to turn and evade easier or jump farther, ect. 
I wish this game had a feedback space but I understand why not. But their roadmap setup on trello definitely makes things easier to understand, it was fairly difficult to find a discord link that wasn't expired to get more information on this game. 

Despite the new games coming out, Animalia is still the best african species survival game so if you can handle dying to unfair players and natural reasons on occasion and a glitch or lag here and there, go ahead and get it. I have fun more than not in this game when I do play, just be sure to read the rules of the server you're joining.

Now that I've sunk some hours into the game *coughs*...a few hundred. I have a few things to say before anyone actually buys the game.
THE GOOD:
-The graphics are beautiful if your compute can handle it.
-The player base as a whole is mostly good, chaotic good or neutral.
-There are ton of helpful people who are willing to stop what they are doing (even those of use who are not admin) to help someone who is just learning the game.
-If you like a challenge, you'll love this.

THE BAD:
-Some of the game mechanics are still very broken. You will get stuck. You will get frustrated with them.
-The players who don't fit into the categories mentioned above can make game play very difficult. You will spend some time in tickets. You will get murdered, a lot.

OVERALL: If you are mature enough to accept defeat, mechanical flaws and general aggravation without being disrespectful, lashing out or rage quitting...you'll be just fine. My biggest advice for new players is to NOT LET OTHERS CONTROL YOUR EMOTIONS. Do not let someone else ruin your gaming experience because that's a THEM problem, not you a YOU problem. Just take a deep breath and try again. Eventually, you will find a good group to play with daily and you will enjoy the time you spend here with the rest of us.

I have seen a ton of unhelpful reviews on this game that are definitely dragging it down and warding potential players away from it, and the content it has to offer. 
I've played it for near 70 hours so far because I wanted to get more of a grasp before reviewing it. I have that grasp now. There are pros, and obviously there are cons. In my opinion, I think the pros definitely outweigh the cons. (which you're entitled to not give a crap about.) 

I've seen a few reviews where people have compared the game to The Isle. I'm a player of The Isle, and I acknowledge the similarities, but I've noticed similarities to games like Beast of Bermuda as well. Animalia so far has proven to be well-rounded. The models are not mind-blowing but they're amazing for a game in it's stage. The graphics aren't mind-blowing but they're also amazing for a game in it's stage.

The enviroment is something I have never seen before. I love the diversity of areas and how big it is. One thing that amazes me is the water mechanic. When drinking, water will go down, which can result in a dry season. I have never seen something like that before, and it is amazing. It also puts in a bit more realism to the game. 

Now, I see a lot of complaints about the toxicity of servers, but- it all depends. I've found amazing servers and have had fun campaigns. Of course there's rulebreakers, it's a newer game, there's going to be new players. It's frustrating sometimes, but staff and admin of servers can help you.

Overall, I love this game. I'm so excited to see where it goes.

I bought one of them (the EggHunt one) and for almost 20.-, you only have one new playable animal, one bunny ears (cosmetic) and 2 new save slots. It's nothing. And it's worse for the other DLCs where you don't even have a new playable animal. You only have cosmetics and skins. 
    [*]The main menu is neither good looking nor intuitive. When you press a button, the color doesn't change, so you don't know if the button is selected or not. Also, the first time I played, I didn't have any sound. You have to activate the sounds yourself in the settings. In the animal creation menu, it seems you can change the physical appearance of your animal, but it doesn't work when you try. And the first time I played, I spent a lot of time trying to understand why I couldn't spawn my animal: that was because I chose a skin with a little diamond above it, which mean I have to pay to use it. But there were no indication that I couldn't use it. 
    [*]When you spawn, you start as a baby and you don't have much to do during the growing phase. If you were born in a family, it's better. But still, it's often boring to grow. You just wait in a safe spot and be afk until you're adult. Once you're adult, you can hunt, travel, mate and start a family and take care of your babies. But as a baby, you're too weak to do anything, so you just hide and wait. However, the good thing is that the more people you have in your group, the faster you'll grow. 
    [*]There is no tutorial. I think that's really a shame, because there are a lot of content and game mecanics that players don't even know about, just because there is no information about them. For exemple, as a warthog or meerkat, you can dig by pressing C at specific places. Or as a leopard, you can climb trees once you're sub-adult. But how are you supposed to know all that if nothing is said about it? Most of the things I know about the game, I've learned it from other players. I think it's a real shame, because a lot of players think that there aren't a lot of game mechanics in the game, when in fact there are a lot of them. 
[/list] 

[h3] Positive points: [/h3]
[list]
    [*]The community is very friendly and helpful. If you're a new player, you will always find someone willing to help you learn the game. I've never had a bad experience. And I also always try myself to help new players when I can. Also, I know there are people who complain about the rules in the most active server, but the rules are there to protect players from other players while keeping a realistic experience as an wild animal. I'm pretty glad there are those rules, because without them, the game would have been awful to play. Plus, the rules make sense for a realistic experience. 
    [*]The map is huge. There are a lot of beautiful places to discover and different biomes (savannah, jungle, desert, caves, etc.). I love to travel with my group. Also, as an herbivore, you will travel more as you have to find safe places, away from predators, to raise your babies. 
    [*]You can make your own build for your animal as you have skill points to spend in different things such as health, armor, stamina, attack, water, food, oxygen, fortitude (for protection against temperatures), etc. Each animal has basic stats and you can build your own stats on them. 
    [*]Each animal has their own characteristics/abilities. Rhinos can charge, crocs can detect animals from underwater and grab them, hyenas make a lot of bleedings when attacking, gazelles are fast, giraffes can eat leaves from trees and they break their legs easily, meerkats and warthog can dig and eat insects, hippos and crocs can stay longer underwater without breathing, male lions and wild dogs can become elder, birds can fly and make nests, leopards can climb, etc. 
    [*]The water dries when players drink. You have to wait until it rains for the lakes to fill up again or you can travel to find water. I think it's a pretty unique and realistic game mechanic. 
[/list] 

Also, you have to be aware that the devs are currently working on a new version of Animalia as they wanted to work on a fresh start to get rid of the bugs in the game. This new version will be crossplatform. You already can test the beta if you own Animalia. There will be more mechanics and new animals such as cheetahs and snakes.

Jump has no animation (though the assets that were used have SEVERAL jump animations, why they weren't used at all is a mystery), and on top of it, it seems jumping has quite a delay, and jumping while standing doesn't function properly. Sprinting feels okay thankfully. Trot feels a bit broken at the moment, at least for Jaguar.

Early access, in my opinion, just does not feel like an excuse for some of these issues. It feels lazy and rushed out. Had there had been a bit more polish and thought put into the player experience, I may not be complaining.

I was glad to see character customization (the camera during character customization felt super clunky unfortunately) and character stats, it's nice to see some sort of extra progression in addition to simply aging to adulthood. I'm grateful that carnivore food sources are available even when people are offline, however, the AI that I did see didn't seem to react in any way to carnivore players, nor did I see them even move.

A lot of game breaking bugs right now. Drinking lasts indefinitely and there's no way to cancel the action. It seems eating does too, but at the very least it's canceled when the corpse disappears (I think?). It's unclear what's buggy due to networking or buggy due to bad code and lack of testing.

I really like the concept of this game, it's something I've wanted to be developed for a long time, the devs have done well so far and I'm glad someone has taken this project on so I don't want to be harsh as I don't think it's deserved.

Pros:

I like the range of animals (more will be added) with their customisation options as well as the life stages, and the inclusion of flying animals which I think they've done an amazing job with, the feather animations are particularly good. The graphics are nice and the lighting and skybox is amazing, and the underwater animations and sound were solid. Some people have said they weren't able to play as elephants but I was able to play as all species available currently including elephants, some just don't have other life stages beyond adult right now. Global chat is helpful and a feature that should stay, don't take it out like Evirma did. The map is large and though I didn't explore all of it, it seems diverse in landscape, the load in region selector is solid. There were more people playing than I expected there to be and servers have a high capacity which is good and hopefully will be more populated in the future.

That being said there's still a long way to go - as is expected in an early access game. 

It's taken clear inspiration from The Isle which is a step in the right direction for this kind of animal simulator, but needs some polish. The mating system will be interesting but I didn't get a chance to try it out. 

Cons: 

Running feels more like drifting across the floor, the turning is a bit clunky and the animal sounds clip in and out in an unnatural way, some species are also missing some of the different calls but it's still early days so I don't fault that too much and I'm sure they'll be added and changed. The combat so far isn't much different from other games like this, your basic left and right mouse click attacks. There is very little in the way of world sound and the night vision is.. interesting, it illuminates your character with a spotlight but that's about it so doesn't make navigating in the dark much easier but that could be a purposeful choice. I couldn't tell if there was NPC's or not, there was lots of bodies on the floor which were still alive but looked to be dying so I don't know if they were the bodies of players that had respawned to test other animals or not. I've had this game for years. I played it back when it was in its prime around 2021-2022. I ended up taking a multi-year break from the game and have come back to it recently (May 15th) and I enjoyed it. HOWEVER, as is always the case with this game, they rolled out new updates and completely broke the game - AGAIN. The players are just completely sick of this. They added Anti-Cheat software AND now have forced the players to login using their Epic Games login account for "Crossplay" - the whole reason I'm on Steam is because I prefer playing on Steam, why would you force us to use MORE third-party software???
The graphics have taken a MASSIVE nosedive from when I first played years ago and even the menus are incredibly laggy. For context, on full mouse sensitivity, it still takes a good second for the mouse to cross from one side of the screen to the other. The models glitch and bug out way too easily, and the servers are complete rubbish, or the game just refuses to show them on the server list.
Some of the animals feel balanced, but others completely aren't. They recently introduced the python - which sounds awesome - until you realise it's completely useless. Most servers need to have extremely strict rules in order to keep things fair, because otherwise the majority of animals other than lions, leopards and zebras can't survive. I was only able to survive as a hippo (pre-game-breaking update) because I just camped out in a watering hole and grew by myself - which isn't a great way to play a MULTI-PLAYER game.

This game should NOT be sold in its current state. It is a broken, horridly buggy mess. The devs refuse to listen to the community, so most of the players have already left. Most of us are waiting for Untamed Kingdom. Hopefully some competition will get the devs to care about this game again.

Edit: Checked back in after a while (11/11/2025) - it's still a broken mess. Another thing I realised as well, the game isn't balanced properly AT ALL. You can tell that no effort went into the other animals aside from lions and leopards. Hippos don't have a swim animation - they literally just float through the water, the elephants are easy to take down because their animations are too slow, so two lions can take down an elephant, which is just not realistic at all (or fun tbh). And another thing, this game basically forces you to be either a lion or a leopard because playing as anything else puts an immediate target on your back and, due to the aforementioned poor game design, they can just put all their points into attack and kill you with no trouble whatsoever. There's also no rules regarding mix-packing - or rather, no rule enforcement regarding it. And if someone DOES break the rules, there's no way to report them in-game, so, I was stuck with people calling each other slurs in the game chat and who were admitting to falsely reporting people in the Discord server, and there was nothing you could do about it (since the admin don't really care and even super-serious offences only result in a mere 30-day ban anyway).

TLDR 2: This boring, buggy game is filled with toxic, bored players who abuse the game's poor design to bully others. Maybe I'll check back in in a couple months, but honestly? I'd rather not.

I see that very recently crocodile was added as a playable and that there are two dlcs (christmas and skins) already. - Leopard climbing insanely broken (Don't even understand why it was added in this state tbh it is horrific).

- Getting stuck in drinking animation
- Getting stuck in lying animation
- Drinking not working in certain areas of water at all
- textures turning white

In my memory, the olden days of cool and fun animal games were Lif, iPredator, and WolfQuest. For ages, many (including myself) been needing and searching for an animal game of potential and quality. We've got these cool dinosaur games... granted the community sucks on those games, but it has opened the realm for better and more improved versions as well as opened the pool for life simulation games such as an animal survival game.

I am sad to say... this is not the game that I look upon to hold great potential or quality. I genuinely regret purchasing it.

Judging for an early access game.. I am not impressed. 

- It is riddled with bugs which is not a surprise however if you are currently looking for a nice game to chill and just be immersed in being an animal, these bugs will ABSOLUTELY take you out of the immersion. The interaction is sometimes unresponsive and god, the eating of the meat is hellish. You grab a piece of it and it starts to ragdol and fly around like you just killed a dinosaur on Ark and it glitched around; that is this but consistently.
- For a game claiming to be towards realism, the DLCs (money-grab) and the inability to remove people's funky looking hats and heart glasses, definitely do not - in any way, shape, or form - advertise as such.
- The voting of features that ARE fundamental to the game yet are treated as merely a suggestion is worrying for a game that is currently beyond unbalanced. The latency, speed, rubberbanding during fighting is unplayable for some including myself and for others it's.. meh. For me, it is an absolute turn off. I don't even bother with the combat in this game, it has just left a horrible taste in my mouth.
- For some, the animations are great. Personally, I feel they are lacking and so my immersion breaks when playing this game. I feel it could use more time and weight to the animations. Everything feels as if its almost light weight and it can start actually flying at any second.
- The game seems pretty dead to say the least, it could just be the times that I got on just sucked, however I have been on when its been populated and barely populated. Even when its populated, the current map is so large, you get lost, you can absolutely be alone for the entirety of your time playing or finally run into someone or do the fast method of accepting an invite to being a baby and hopefully being able to grow with your group as some just straight up log once you join. It can be very very fun with this community but it all depends on timing. This game when playing alone is quite honestly unplayable. It feels bland, gets very boring... these types of games run based on the community. The community is what drives this game to function and do what it needs to do: act like an animal survival game. It is what makes it feel alive, real, and thriving. That is one of the major downfalls of these kinds of games which I feel can be alleviated with including other options or features.

I wanted to enjoy this game. I felt no reason to come back but tried it for one last time and... personally I can not love this game or like it very much. I do not recommend it in it's current state and can only hope that one day.. 5 years from now or hopefully sooner, who knows, it can and will get better.

Rating: ★☆☆☆☆ (1/5)

Animalia promised to let you be African animals in a survival game on the savannah, but it falls way short of its big promises. This game, aiming for a multiplayer world where animals fight to survive, is full of big problems that make it more frustrating than fun.

First, the way the animals move is just weird. Whether you're a fast gazelle or a big elephant, the movements are jerky and awkward, making it hard to feel like you're really the animal.
The game is all about survival, but it's not fair. Some animals like the leopard and lion are way too strong, making the game feel like a mess. There's not enough variety in the animals' abilities, so playing smart or being creative isn't really an option.
The designs of the animals don't capture the beauty of African wildlife. They seem rushed and not well thought out. It's like the creators didn't pay attention to how real animals look and feel.
The game keeps getting updates with new animals, but it doesn't really help. The main problems don't get fixed, and it feels like they're just trying to cover up the issues instead of making the game better.
The developers don't seem to care about what players think. They don't listen to feedback, and that's made the community toxic, with a lot of frustration and disappointment.
On top of all that, the game has technical problems. It's hard to move around because of low frames and lag. This just adds to the game's problems.

In the end, Animalia is a big disappointment. The bad movements, unfair gameplay, boring designs, and ignoring player feedback make it a really unsatisfying game. Until they make it a lot better, I wouldn't recommend wasting your time on this not-so-great safari.

The best way that I can describe this game is instant regret. This game's developers appear to be from the community of another game called The Isle. Some of their devs were apparently admins on an old isle server called Rogue Realism. I suspect it is because of these people and the biased opinions that they formed from the other game that makes this game such trash. In my opinion the game is extremely unpolished, clunky, chock full of bugs, and heavily in favor of the carnivore faction. It makes the same mistakes of Isle Legacy where a$$riding is the favoured mode of combat. 

The combat is cartoonishly bad and the animations are janky and unrealistic. The balance is so bad that a single male lion can stun lock an animal like a rhino with slappy paws and shred through an adult elephant like its skin is made of paper. The devs have an unrealistic view of carnivores and seem to think that a single male lion should be able to stack up 10 pile high bodies of elephants. Realistically, the only animal capable of doing that irl are humans with guns. If we take a look at realistic hunting rates, which the devs try to use to claim to back up their bias, the lion has a relatively low success rate when compared with other carnivores as referenced here: https://www.discoverwildlife.com/animal-facts/mammals/hunting-success-rates-how-predators-compare/

The game seems to be a shallow attempt at making playable african animals with minimal effort all for the sake of profit, while being a time sink with no true goal outside of that fact. Save yourself some time and money and treat yourself to something nice instead. This is probably one of the worst purchase's I've ever made and I regret everything. How they managed to take what seemed like such a cool concept and then botch it this badly is beyond me. In conclusion, I'd recommend not touching this game or its seemingly biased shady devs with a 10 foot pole.

I am a long time player with over 380 hours clocked. I started this game for the humor but fell in love with the community and although imperfect I could easily look past it and found myself lounging on rocks, exploring, chatting, and hunting for hours. I have gotten to know so many players and have even gained friends along the way. Getting excited to see each new animal and update, but with that being said I cannot sadly, recommend this game. 

For the reasons following: 
- [b]With every new update, one or more features break and they are fixed at slow pace if at all.[/b]
  - Ex. Crocodiles added -> Birds broke, they can no longer grab animals (food) a vital feature for their survival. It has been months with still no fix or word on them.
- [b]Rushes to push animals out with out fixing previous issues or animals.[/b] 
  - Animals being shoved out unpolished often with balancing issues and or broken features which they slightly band-aid but never fully fix, just enough to get by. This leads to over powered or under powered glitchy animals. It often feels like many things are not tested before they are released.
   - Ex. leopards have a climbing feature that was added many months ago but you will find yourself struggling to scale rocks and trees unless you hit things /just/ right. Terribly dangerous if you have predators chasing you. Crocodiles are over powered still, able to take down full elephants and hippos hitting for over 3k damage at times. 
- [b]Lion Favoritism[/b]
  - This game heavily leans towards lions as the favorites, they are terribly unbalanced and a few elders can easily take on full grown elephants, crocodiles, hippos, leopards, you name it. When we know that is not something even vaguely possible with out lions paying dearly in the wild. 
- [b]Playing as a Herbivore is not fun.[/b] 
  - This game makes playing as a herbivore absolutely miserable, they designed zebras and wildebeest to be practically made of glass even with moving your stats around. When they are able to deal some hearty damage in real life. You will not get that strong, powerful, herbivore feel in this game. Even as elephants, rhinos, and hippos...if you have a crocodile or two chasing you or a few lions you are typically toast as they pursue you to the end of the map.
- [b]Privately hosted servers with house rules made on the spot and often admins playing favorites.[/b]
  - If you are still determined to buy this, be prepared to have only one or two populated servers to pick from with rules you will not know with out joining their Discords. You will get scolded and dragged if you break one even if you are brand new more often than not. This often chases new players away who arrive, spawn in and explore and fight back when they are suddenly attacked not quite knowing the rules of engagement yet. Also be prepared for heavy favoritism as admins do their best to turn blind eyes or defend the regular favorites even if they break said rules and run to their aid when they claim you broke one. It is a very disheartening feeling as you try your best to explain your side but the favorite's voices are always louder leading to an unhealthy community as of late.

So overall, despite all the time I have poured into this game and the memories I have I cannot recommend it for these reasons. But I will always treasure the little memories I do hold with it from earlier days and hopes one day it will better but that is looking bleak.

First, my preface; I have been playing Animalia since about a year after it released, albeit not over a large number of hours. I play every few updates to see what has changed over time. For animal survival games, my go-to is The Isle, but I was hoping Animalia would provide a slightly less intense experience. However, thus far the result has been disappointing.

1) The game isn't the best looking or moving. The static elements of the game look just fine, but it's the player models, the things which are most important and you spend the most time looking at, which need serious work. Every single model has something wrong with it either in the way it moves or the way it looks. The transitions between gates are either slowed down to allow for a transitional animation that isn't there or jolt you into the next gear like a stick shift that's transmission is about to go out. Jumping is an awful affair on animals that have it. Swimming is stupidly slow and difficult. And with the new O2 system, you're more likely to drown than make it across a river that wouldn't be that hard to cross otherwise. Also due to the O2 system, Crocs can barely stay underwater, meaning you can't get the jump on players coming to take a drink. Climbing with leopards is a tedious affair. Most trees aren't meshed for it and those that are have such spotty meshes that it's hard to tell whether your leopard is going to fall through the branch or glide a few feet in the air but still technically be on the tree. Forget about actually hunting from up there! You're completely visible to all players on the sparsely foliated trees, and if that wasn't enough; you can't control where you're going to land when you jump down in addition to leopards not having a vertical pounce attack in the first place.

2) The map is almost completely empty. If you're buying this game to explore a beautiful map and see all the unique locations the creators have built, please take your expectations down a notch. The map that is currently available is more akin to the Day of Dragons map than that of The Isle: EVRIMA. There are vast swaths of badlands where no players ever go, or are ever incentivized to go. There are only a few locations where everyone tends to congregate, meaning you have to hang around those locations as well if you either want A. to interact with another player on the map or B. ever want to find food as a predator. There is a large jungle canyon network on the map that can take an hour or two to get out of if you don't know the way. It would be fun if you had a chance at encountering something scary there, but most players steer clear of it after getting lost in there once or twice with no food or water.

3) The game doesn't feed carnivores. One crucial aspect of a survival game is feeding predators via NPCs when they are nearly starving due to either a lack of other, weaker players around, the player actively hiding from another, stronger player, or other such circumstances. Animalia just doesn't have this. Dotted around the map are carcasses which sort of serve this purpose, but are once again just opportunities for players to congregate and chit chat IMVU style. There's no experience of trudging through the badlands and spotting a lizard in the distance that might just carry you over till you get to the other side. There's no nearly starving as a juvenile but finally managing to catch that smaller mammal you've been working on for half an hour. There's no experience of sitting in a bush as a young bachelor lion at night in a foreign pride's territory and them locating you via the gazelle the game spawned to quiet your growling stomach. There's no learning to fish as a croc, even, because they added playable crocs before adding AI fish for them to eat. AI has been introduced by server modders, but the tiny affect their mods add to the game does not make up for the massive hole in the fabric these developers are trying to weave. The developers have mentioned AI several times, to my knowledge through rumor, yet have chosen to add multiple new species to the game instead on claims that the AI is taking longer to develop. Well, I think I speak for most of the player base in that we'd rather get bare bones AI into the game over another shoddy animal model which adds no value or playability to the game.

4) Combat is... strange. Fighting carnivore v carnivore (or non-tank herbie) in this game is just a game of who has the smaller ping at the end of the day. Whomever can keep on target, without hitting a lag spike, wins. The combat in this game is just so different to the nature it's trying to emulate. The predators don't jump on the prey, the prey have absolutely no defenses at all, there's no incentive for herd animals to stay together when attacked, there's no opportunities for predators to ambush prey, carnivores don't duke it out in close combat when encountering one another. I could go on and on about how the system is lacking, but it's safe to say it's bare bones. 

5) Most servers are empty, and those that aren't just serve as chatrooms. In 69 hours of playing this game, only a few have been in "survival" mode. 90% of the time, this game functions more like a Beasts of Bermuda event without any of the fun or payoff for your time. Some servers host breeding "events" but these events mostly just consist of sitting around and waiting for your character to get hungry, thirsty, or randomly attacked by another bored player. For the remaining 10% of play, the game is frustrating, but can be entertaining when the action picks up.

6) Slow as molasses development. It has been a LONG time since this game received a major update. Most updates in the last few months have consisted of "tweaks" and bug fixing. Every now and again, a new playable species will be added. However, it is usually followed by months of balance patching and 

7) DLC. This game has $55 USD worth of DLC in its current state. DLC which adds nothing more than skins and items to the game, mind you. For a game with so many unfinished features, buggy mechanics, and absolutely nothing to do, that's a ton of money, plus purchasing the game itself. To me, it seams the developers are much more focused on selling items microtransaction-style than actually buckling down and working out the features that are supposed to have at least made visible progress in the game by now. Instead, the most recent update as of this writing (03/31/2023) has actually [b] REMOVED [/b] the weather and wateringhole leveling systems from the game. I'm sorry, but you have officially irritated me as a customer when you remove features with no explanation or timeline of replacement in the patch notes, but also want to make me pay $13 USD for a few Halloween costumes my character can wear.

TL;DR: This game has a long way to go before it is worth the initial buy in, and a hell of a lot further to go before it's worth the DLC money out of your wallet. I would stick this game on your Wishlist and come back in 2025 or 2026. If the world hasn't gone to sh*t, maybe this game will be worth playing by then.
